ExplanationParts.CorpusEarnedOpening: Going to hell like an arrow is a rapid and emphatic adverse verdict on a claimed way of seeing or understanding a case.
EvidenceBody: Cian Shoujing gives the phrase its sharpest two-sided form: taking Linji’s event as a blow and not taking it as a blow receive the identical verdict. Shexian Guisheng twice applies it even to claimed understanding. Tiantong Jie aims it at a proposed awakening by five hundred monks, Yunfeng Wenyue at the student’s reading of Zhaozhou’s bowl case, and Ruiyan Rusheng at anyone who claims to see his staff presentation.

DraftEvidence.ZenBend: A familiar hell warning becomes a public interview veto that can close both offered interpretations instead of supplying a safer doctrinal answer.
DraftEvidence.CounterexampleOrLimit: The phrase does not prove a literal postmortem destination or identify one correct opposite; the doubled and “even if” constructions show it functioning as a present verdict on the proposed reading.

ComparedThings: go to hell like an arrow
the same expression in questions, answers, comments, and verdicts
DifferentThingTest.Reason: The double blow/no-blow veto witness and the staff-presentation veto control change the phrase’s public job without producing a different referent.

DraftEvidence.AliasRationale: The lookup wording follows the understanding still condemned deployment and remains bounded by the preferred target.

ModifierControls.reason: The second no-substitute warning witness supplies no material relation requiring a color-or-substance branch.

FamilyControls.reason: The staff-presentation veto control keeps the neighboring expressions 地獄, 不昧因果, 錯會 outside this evidence count.

DeploymentClassAudit.Reason: Parallel recensions were excluded from depth.
